messages:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT RESOLVED]  prod-inference kv-cache corruption detected -> auto-fallback triggered. Impact window 03:12-03:27 UTC. Affected: request latency spikes, some 500s for long-context sharded requests. Logs: https://logs.redwood.example/incident/1958123456 :eyes:

alex: thanks bot. can we use this thread to schedule a postmortem + track action items? tagging folks who were on-call last night @jamie @mira @sre_lead

jamie: I can start. tl;dr — mem corruption on shard-02 due to concurrent cache flush + migration job. mitigation was to disable auto-flush and route traffic to fallback model variants. restarted shard after kv rehydrate.

mira: got it. I'll own the postmortem doc and runbook edits unless someone else wants it. propose 1hr slot today or tomorrow for async writeup + 30m sync. who can make room? @alex @jamie

sre_lead: +1 for owning remediation tracker in tracker board. we should also capture customer impact and whether to trigger SLA outreach. @product-eric 

alex: customer impact summary for the doc: ~120 requests failed (4xx/5xx), 3 paying customers saw degraded response times, no data loss. preliminary severity: Sev2.

jamie: adding the short playbook steps I ran — put here so we can codify: ```bash
# quick mitigation commands run during incident
# 1. disable auto-flush for kv-cache on cluster
kubectl -n inference patch configmap kv-cache-config -p '{"data":{"autoFlush":"false"}}'
# 2. set routing weight to fallback model
curl -X POST https://controlplane/redwood/routing -d '{"route":"fallback","weight":1.0}'
# 3. restart shard-02
kubectl -n inference rollout restart ds/kv-shard-02
```

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline CI: inference/kv-cache-patch succeeded (build #8432) :rocket:

product-eric: thanks — product needs a short customer note. prelim draft: "We observed an availability issue affecting inference latency for a small subset of requests between 03:12–03:27 UTC. Traffic was routed to a fallback model while we repaired the service. No customer data was lost. We're updating our runbooks and adding safeguards to prevent recurrence." will post to affected customers after PM sync.

mira: proposed meeting windows: today 17:00 UTC (preferred), tomorrow 11:00 UTC, OR async writeup in doc. I'll create a calendar invite once we decide.

alex: I can do 17:00. jamie?

jamie: 17:00 works. I'll bring the debug timeline and logs.

sre_lead: action items (high-level) — assign owners in tracker: 1) root cause analysis + RCA writeup (mira) 2) runbook update: disable auto-flush migration gating + explicit migration window (alex) 3) add healthcheck + alert for kv rehydrate failures (jamie) 4) postmortem review w/ product + customer comms (product-eric) 5) SLA impact review and billing/credit consideration (sre_lead). please confirm owners.

alex: confirmed for runbook update. I'll add a checklist entry: - add pre-migration gating flag - require dry-run healthcheck pass - add step to pause auto-flush during migration.

jamie: I'll add the healthcheck — suggested probe: after shard restart, run kv-hash-verify and kv-consistency-check. I'll add alerts if verify fails 3x within 5m.

oncall-bot: Reminder: postmortem template is at https://wiki.redwood/postmortems/template. Please fill sections: timeline, impact, root cause, corrective actions, preventive actions, owners, verification plan.

product-eric: for customer comms I'll prepare a targeted message for the 3 paying customers and a general status note for status.redwood.ai. will share drafts in the doc before send.

mira: created postmortem doc draft: https://wiki.redwood/postmortems/1958123456-kv-cache. starting with timeline — please paste any logs or short snippets directly into the doc. I'll collate.

alex: one more runbook gap we found: no explicit fallback gating for quantized vs fp32 model variants. I'll add that to the runbook update task.

sre_lead: good catch. add task: "routing policy: prefer variant with KV-tolerance; fallback only if latency < X ms" — owner: alex.

jamie: question re: SLA — do we trigger automatic credits for >5m degraded in highest tier? I thought policy was 10m.

sre_lead: policy is 10m for automatic credits; we'll review case-by-case for these customers since 15m window had partial degradation for them. I'll start the review.

mira: final checklist for sync: - meet 17:00 UTC (link in invite) - owners confirmed above - postmortem doc linked - product to draft comms - engineering to update runbook + add healthchecks - follow-up verification in 2 weeks. anyone object?

alex: no objections. thanks all. adding tasks to the oncall board.

jamie: will paste timeline + logs into the doc before the meeting. last note: we saw a noisy migration job scheduled concurrently by infra-team; need to add a preflight check to scheduler. adding to runbook tasks.

oncall-bot: Created task card: "1958123456 - KV-cache postmortem & runbook updates" -> https://tracker.redwood/board/cards/5692 assigned to mira, alex, jamie, product-eric, sre_lead.

mira: perfect. I'll run the sync and put the runbook PR in the eng repo after we agree on wording. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
